loop_tick_ms.description: Period in milliseconds at which the virtual actuation board (pkg/boardsim) steps boardloop. Emulates the firmware's loop rate; read only in simulation, never by a real board.

seed.description: Seed of the link emulation's jitter and byte corruption, so a simulated run repeats.

to_board.description: Emulation of the host-to-board direction of the link (Config, Command, Ping).

latency_ms.description: Fixed delay in milliseconds added to every chunk of bytes sent to the board.

jitter_ms.description: Maximum extra delay in milliseconds, drawn uniformly per chunk; chunks are never reordered.

corrupt_rate.description: Probability per byte that one random bit is flipped, to exercise the boardlink decoder's resynchronization.

loss_rate.description: Long-run fraction of chunks lost whole, in bursts (Gilbert-Elliott); 0 disables loss.

loss_burst.description: Mean number of consecutive chunks lost once a loss starts; 1 gives independent losses. Read only when loss_rate is set.

stall_rate_hz.description: Average number of stalls starting per second (Poisson); 0 disables random stalls.

stall_ms.description: How long each stall holds delivery, in milliseconds; what was sent meanwhile arrives together when it ends, as a stuck USB endpoint's backlog does.

to_host.description: Emulation of the board-to-host direction of the link (Hello, Status, Odometry, Button, Pong).

latency_ms.description: Fixed delay in milliseconds added to every frame the board sends.

jitter_ms.description: Maximum extra delay in milliseconds, drawn uniformly per frame; frames are never reordered.

corrupt_rate.description: Probability per byte that one random bit is flipped, to exercise the host's boardlink decoder.

loss_rate.description: Long-run fraction of chunks lost whole, in bursts (Gilbert-Elliott); 0 disables loss.

loss_burst.description: Mean number of consecutive chunks lost once a loss starts; 1 gives independent losses. Read only when loss_rate is set.

stall_rate_hz.description: Average number of stalls starting per second (Poisson); 0 disables random stalls.

stall_ms.description: How long each stall holds delivery, in milliseconds; what was sent meanwhile arrives together when it ends, as a stuck USB endpoint's backlog does.
